This appeal having been heard and reserved for orders, coming on for pronouncement this day, this court passed the following:

ORDER Appellant/Insurance Company has filed this appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 assailing the impugned award dated 6/9/2022 passed by Sixth Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena, District Morena (M.P.) whereby, respondent No. 1/claimant has been awarded a compensation of Rs. 3,36,000/- alongwith interest at the rate of 6% per annum and liability of payment of compensation was fixed upon appellant and respondent no. 2 and 3 jointly and severelly.
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Morena, District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This appeal is filed solely on the ground that on the date of incident i.e. 3/7/2018, driver of offending dumber i.e. respondent no. 2 was not holding valid driving licence and to support this contention, appellant has filed copy of report of RTO, Morena alongwith an application vide I.A.No.
3272/2023, which is an application under Order XLI Rule 27 CPC read with Section 169 of MV Act for taking documents on record.
3. Since factum of accident is not disputed by offending vehicle, the entire story need not be reiterated.
4. Learned counsel for the respondent No. 1 by filing cross objections prayed for enhancement of the impugned award by a further sum of Rs. 50,000/-.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.
6. I.A.No. 3272/2023 is allowed since the document filed with this application is necessary for just decision of the appeal.

A perusal of document i.e. report of RTO, Morena dated 17/8/2021 makes it clear that on the date of incident i.e. 3/7/2018, driver i.e. respondent no. 2 was not holding valid driving licence to drive heavy motor vehicle and same was acquired by him on 24/7/2018 whereas,
incident took place on 3/7/2018 and therefore, it appears that it is only after the incident took place,
respondent No. 2 applied for driving licence to driver heavy motor vehicle.
Therefore in the opinion of this Court, learned Claims Tribunal erred in fastening the liability of payment of compensation amount over the Insurance Company.

sentences.text: As regards cross-objections filed on behalf of respondent No. 1, in the opinion of this Court the amount of compensation so awarded by the Claims Tribunal is just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case and needs no enhancement.
8. Cumulatively, appeal filed by appellant-Insurance Company is allowed and cross-objectiosn filed by respondent no. 1 are rejected.

Appellant-Insurance Company is exempted from making payment of compensation amount and instead respondents No. 2 and 3 are held liable for payment of compensation amount since at the time of incident, respondent No. 2 was not having valid driving licence to driver heavy motor vehicle.

However, in the facts and circumstances of the case,
appellant/Insurance Company is directed to make the payment of compensation amount to respondent No. 1/claimant, if not already paid, and thereafter recover the same from respondents No. 2 and 3.
Let payment of compensation amount be made within two months.
9. Accordingly, appeal stands allowed and disposed of.

(AVANINDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE jps/-
